source_name: Money.hu Tudástár
why_relevant: Knowledge-base arm of a HU financial comparison brand; maintains evergreen explainers on cash-withdrawal rules and limits (e.g. the 2026 HUF 300,000 free monthly limit) that are updated as regulation changes — a cheap way to timestamp HU retail payment rule changes.

source_name: Bankkártya.hu
why_relevant: Niche HU card-industry site that has published side-by-side comparisons of POS terminal operators' offers — acquirer pricing/market-structure data that no official source aggregates. Domain name is the core local term for the sector.

source_name: Origo — gazdaság (ATM network coverage)
why_relevant: High-reach general portal that covers the state-driven restructuring of the Hungarian ATM network (ATM rollout targets for small settlements, cash-services consolidation). Policy-adjacent cash-infrastructure signals often appear here and in county papers before specialist outlets.

source_name: Sonline.hu and the Mediaworks county-daily network
why_relevant: County dailies syndicate national copy on ATM/cash-service changes and add local detail on terminal deployments in small settlements — the only granular geographic signal on HU cash-access infrastructure. Observed piece on ATMs being replaced by new cash-service terminals.

source_name: Deloitte Magyarország – Insights / Perspectives (Consulting, Financial Services)
why_relevant: Deloitte Hungary publishes Hungarian-language thought-leadership on digital banking, payment habits and customer preferences, including local commentary on the global Digital Banking Maturity study. These are primary-survey-based outputs not derivable from MNB statistics.

source_name: Deloitte Digital Hungary – legacy article archive (www2.deloitte.com/hu)
why_relevant: Older Deloitte Digital Hungary articles on digital sales/channel maturity of banks still live on the legacy www2 domain; useful for time series of the Digital Banking Maturity results for Hungary. Note ongoing migration from www2 to www — old links may redirect.

source_name: PwC Magyarország – Sajtószoba (press room) / Digitális Pénzügyi Körkép
why_relevant: PwC Hungary runs its own large-N primary survey 'Digitális Pénzügyi Körkép' on digital payment solutions and consumer choice (reported >3,300 quantitative respondents plus ~20 interviews). Directly on-topic for payment behaviour and cash-vs-digital substitution.

source_name: PwC Hungary – English site (pwc.com/hu/en)
why_relevant: English mirror of PwC Hungary publications; useful when HU-only press releases have an EN counterpart and for CEE-level banking/payments studies with Hungary breakouts.

source_name: KPMG Hungary – Financial Services / Pénzügyi szolgáltatások insights
why_relevant: KPMG Hungary's FS practice publishes sector commentary, regulatory analysis and periodic market studies (incl. fintech/digitalisation) aimed at lead generation; a standing candidate for Hungarian banking market-sizing and payment-digitalisation views.

source_name: GKID (GKI Digital) – research house, e-commerce & payments
why_relevant: GKID is the dominant Hungarian research house for online retail volume and online payment-method split (cash-on-delivery vs card-on-delivery vs online card/transfer). Its releases are the main non-regulator quantitative series on e-commerce payment mix.

source_name: GKID–Mastercard 'Digitális Kereskedelmi Körkép' (ekerkutatas.hu)
why_relevant: Dedicated portal for the GKID–Mastercard e-commerce research programme (successor to the Online Kiskereskedelmi Index), publishing periodic waves with online payment-method shares and shopper-base sizing for Hungary.

source_name: NRC piackutató (NRC Marketingkutató) – online/mobile banking surveys
why_relevant: NRC runs recurring Hungarian online-population surveys covering e-commerce and mobile-banking usage; a research-house primary source on payment/banking channel behaviour independent of the regulator.

source_name: eNET Internetkutató és Tanácsadó Kft.
why_relevant: eNET is a long-standing Hungarian internet-research house whose online-shopping and payment-trust surveys (e.g. cash-on-delivery share) are widely cited; historical waves give a long baseline on cash preference in e-commerce.

source_name: Corvinus Research Archive (unipub.lib.uni-corvinus.hu)
why_relevant: Open institutional repository of Corvinus University of Budapest hosting full-text Hungarian academic work on domestic payment turnover, cash usage and payment habits (incl. Közgazdasági Szemle articles). Searchable, stable, and free — the key academic anchor for this cell.

source_name: Közgazdasági Szemle (Hungarian Economic Review)
why_relevant: Flagship Hungarian peer-reviewed economics journal; publishes academic analyses of payment systems, cash logistics and settlement (authors frequently Corvinus/MNB-affiliated). Peer review gives high credibility for methodology on cash-usage estimates.

source_name: REAL – MTA Könyvtár repozitóriuma (real.mtak.hu)
why_relevant: National open repository of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences library; hosts full texts of Hungarian academic papers on fintech impact on payments, financial literacy and consumer payment behaviour that are otherwise scattered across journals.

source_name: Gazdaság és Pénzügy (Magyar Bankszövetség academic journal)
why_relevant: Peer-reviewed journal of the Hungarian Banking Association carrying academic papers with original survey data on Hungarian fintech and payment adoption (e.g. 'Fintech használat a magyar lakosság körében'). Bridges academia and industry.

source_name: Budapesti Gazdaságtudományi Egyetem (BGE) – research news & Szemelvények series
why_relevant: BGE (formerly Budapest Business School, home of Budapest LAB) publishes applied research on financial literacy, SME finance and payment behaviour; a secondary academic producer beyond Corvinus with a practitioner orientation.

source_name: Neumann János Egyetem (NJE) – doctoral theses & GSZDI repository
why_relevant: NJE's economics doctoral school produces dissertations with original Hungarian consumer surveys on trust in financial services and AI-era banking; theses often contain fieldwork data unavailable elsewhere.

source_name: McKinsey & Company Hungary – Our Insights (Budapest office)
why_relevant: McKinsey's Budapest office publishes Hungarian macro/sector reports (e.g. the 'Repülőrajt' Hungary-2030 study) with banking and digitalisation chapters; also the home of Finalta banking benchmarking, whose public excerpts occasionally cover Hungarian channel/payment metrics.

source_name: EY Magyarország – insights / press
why_relevant: Fourth Big-4 firm in scope for this cell; EY Hungary issues local commentary and occasionally Hungary cuts of global consumer-banking/fintech adoption surveys. Included for completeness — no Hungary-specific payments study was surfaced in this pass.

source_name: FinTechZone.hu
why_relevant: Hungarian fintech trade outlet that systematically reports on consultancy and research-house studies (Deloitte Digital, GKID–Mastercard, PwC) — the fastest way to detect that a new study exists and to recover its headline numbers when the original is gated.

source_name: Digitális Kereskedelmi Szövetség (DKSZ) – research reposts
why_relevant: Hungarian digital commerce association that republishes GKID–Mastercard wave summaries; sometimes hosts material that has been rotated off the researcher's own site, making it a useful mirror/archive for e-commerce payment-mix data.

source_name: HWSW.hu – e-commerce/research archive
why_relevant: Long-running Hungarian tech outlet with a deep archive of eNET and GKI Digital survey coverage going back a decade; the practical way to recover historic payment-method-split figures whose original press releases are no longer online.

source_name: Mastercard Magyarország – Digitális Fizetési Index / Percepciós Index riportok
why_relevant: Mastercard commissions Hungarian survey-based indices (Digitális Fizetési Index, Fenntarthatósági Percepciós Index) executed by local research agencies and publishes full PDF riports. Vendor-sponsored, so treat directionally, but it is genuine Hungarian primary survey data on payment attitudes.

source_name: MNB–Corvinus joint payment-habits studies (MNB Occasional Papers / Hitelintézeti Szemle)
why_relevant: Several key Hungarian academic papers on cash usage and the social cost of payment methods are co-authored by Corvinus researchers but published through MNB channels. For this academic-output cell they are the highest-quality methodological references, even though the host is the regulator.

source_name: Pénzügyi Szemle / Public Finance Quarterly (Állami Számvevőszék)
why_relevant: Peer-reviewed Hungarian public-finance journal that has run focus issues on 'Gazdaság és pénzforgalom' containing academic treatments of payment turnover and cash. Bilingual (HU/EN) which helps cross-language coverage.
